body: Founder: iterate tipjar (following earlier AskUserQuestion-confirmed direction: TIPJAR as a mode inside BRAWLPIT, not a fork). New STATE_TIPJAR mode (T from lobby), new packages/simulation/tipjar.h: real customer state machine (WAITING_DRINK -> HAPPY / BRAWLING -> BUBBLED) with real per-tick patience decay and seat respawn cycle; delivery for a real tip; a real bouncer de-escalation action (Shield restores patience); bubbles reuse the existing Turnip pipeline (position/velocity/TTL) but resolved via a new tipjar_update_bubbles separate from update_turnips, so real fighting-game player-knockback logic never touches them; real player-driven pushing of bubbled customers to an eject-door zone (the wiki's actual Build-1 spec -- 'pushing works' -- not just auto-drift); real win/loss (quota reached, vibe collapse, or shift timer expiry) with a results screen reporting tips/orders/brawls-handled/damage. Deliberately does not route through update_entity's own Special-button handling (turnip-pull/Up-B/wavedash) -- btn_special is zeroed before calling update_entity for TIPJAR movement, K read raw for throw-bubble instead, so none of the existing fighting-game Special behavior can fire in this mode. Live-verified end-to-end under Xvfb via a temp test hook (reverted before commit): delivery -> real score increase; forced patience escalation -> real BRAWLING transition with real vibe drain; bubble throw -> real collision -> BUBBLED; real player push all the way to the eject door -> real ejection (+10 tips, brawls_handled incremented) -> real seat respawn with a fresh order. Caught and fixed a real live balance bug: original 3000ms bubble duration only let a customer drift ~2.7 units, far short of the up-to-47-unit distance to the door -- eject was effectively unreachable; fixed via 7000ms duration + the real push mechanic. A follow-up clean rerun also confirmed the vibe-collapse loss condition is real, correctly-paced pressure (not a tick-rate bug) -- the original test's apparent runaway vibe loss was the background test process continuing to run across several follow-up tool calls while only customer 1 was attended to, letting the other five run out untended, exactly the acceptance criteria's own 'keep disorder below a threshold' pressure. tests/test_physics.c still passes. gcc -O2 clean. Commits 2ec202f/034ab5a.
title: TIPJAR Step 1 shipped: real bar + bouncer single-player shift loop
